# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), adopted in 2024, set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). However, following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package—politically agreed by Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026 and entering into force on 27 July 2026—this date has been amended, and Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to products embedding high-risk AI under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
As originally adopted, the AI Act provided that high-risk AI system obligations, including those in Annex III, would become applicable 36 months after entry into force—around 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Article 113(c), as it stood before the 2026 amendment, set this 2 August 2026 date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3, which govern Annex III high-risk obligations (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, conditional on confirmation that necessary standards and tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Omnibus was reportedly adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the Act's implementation timeline (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Date
As amended, Article 113(c) now provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5))—governing Annex III high-risk systems—shall apply from **2 December 2027** (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). This is corroborated by multiple official EU guidance pages confirming Annex III obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 following the Omnibus's entry into force (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

### Related Timelines
Obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) apply separately, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). Legacy high-risk systems already on the market before the Chapter III application date are only subject to the Act if they undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Separately, Annex III is best understood as a list of use-case categories that *may* be classified high-risk, not an automatic designation (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists regarding whether 2 December 2027 is final: an uncorroborated news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029 (low confidence, flagged below threshold) ([AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)), a claim not supported by any official EU source. Several commentary sources—some undated or predating the Omnibus—continue to cite 2 August 2026 as operative, reflecting outdated information not yet updated post-Omnibus (low-medium confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). An EU guidance page on Article 111 also still references 2 August 2026 as the relevant Chapter III date for legacy systems, seemingly inconsistent with the amended 2 December 2027 date (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). One source describes both dates as "backstop dates" only, implying 2 August 2026 could remain legally operative if Omnibus amendments were not finalized in time (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether 2 December 2027 is truly final or subject to further delay, given the uncorroborated 2029 claim. The precise official citation number of the amending Omnibus regulation is inconsistently reported across sources. It is also unresolved whether all Chapter III, Sections 1–3 provisions share the same 2 December 2027 date, or whether specific sub-provisions (e.g., Article 6(5)) have distinct timelines. Further research is needed on readiness milestones (harmonised standards, notified bodies) required before the date takes effect, and on how guidance will be reconciled across EU sources that have not yet been updated.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The original EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), adopted in 2024, set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). However, following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package—politically agreed by Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026 and entering into force on 27 July 2026—this date has been amended, and Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to products embedding high-risk AI under Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
As originally adopted, the AI Act provided that high-risk AI system obligations, including those in Annex III, would become applicable 36 months after entry into force—around 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Article 113(c), as it stood before the 2026 amendment, set this 2 August 2026 date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3, which govern Annex III high-risk obligations (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months, conditional on confirmation that necessary standards and tools were available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this simplification package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Omnibus was reportedly adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending the Act's implementation timeline (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Date
As amended, Article 113(c) now provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5))—governing Annex III high-risk systems—shall apply from **2 December 2027** (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). This is corroborated by multiple official EU guidance pages confirming Annex III obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 following the Omnibus's entry into force (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)).

### Related Timelines
Obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in products covered by Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) apply separately, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). Legacy high-risk systems already on the market before the Chapter III application date are only subject to the Act if they undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Separately, Annex III is best understood as a list of use-case categories that *may* be classified high-risk, not an automatic designation (low confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists regarding whether 2 December 2027 is final: an uncorroborated news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029 (low confidence, flagged below threshold) ([AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)), a claim not supported by any official EU source. Several commentary sources—some undated or predating the Omnibus—continue to cite 2 August 2026 as operative, reflecting outdated information not yet updated post-Omnibus (low-medium confidence) ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). An EU guidance page on Article 111 also still references 2 August 2026 as the relevant Chapter III date for legacy systems, seemingly inconsistent with the amended 2 December 2027 date (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). One source describes both dates as "backstop dates" only, implying 2 August 2026 could remain legally operative if Omnibus amendments were not finalized in time (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether 2 December 2027 is truly final or subject to further delay, given the uncorroborated 2029 claim. The precise official citation number of the amending Omnibus regulation is inconsistently reported across sources. It is also unresolved whether all Chapter III, Sections 1–3 provisions share the same 2 December 2027 date, or whether specific sub-provisions (e.g., Article 6(5)) have distinct timelines. Further research is needed on readiness milestones (harmonised standards, notified bodies) required before the date takes effect, and on how guidance will be reconciled across EU sources that have not yet been updated.
